{{nihongo|'''Naru Shrine'''|鳴神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kii Province]].

=== Enshrined God ===
The following three deities are currently enshrined. </ref>.
* '''{{ill|Hayakitsuhiko and Hayakitsuhime|fr|Hayakitsuhiko et Hayakitsuhime|ja|ハヤアキツヒコ・ハヤアキツヒメ|ko|하야아키츠히코・하야아키츠히메|simple|Hayaakitsuhiko and Hayaakitsuhime|zh|速秋津日子神與速秋津比賣神|qid=Q11326733|lt=Hayaakitsuhiko no Mikoto}}''' (Hayaakitsuhiko Mikoto) - Left shrine (facing the right shrine).
* '''{{ill|Hayakitsuhiko and Hayakitsuhime|fr|Hayakitsuhiko et Hayakitsuhime|ja|ハヤアキツヒコ・ハヤアキツヒメ|ko|하야아키츠히코・하야아키츠히메|simple|Hayaakitsuhiko and Hayaakitsuhime|zh|速秋津日子神與速秋津比賣神|qid=Q11326733|lt=Hayaakitsuhime no Mikoto}}''' (Hayaakitsuhime Mikoto) - Left shrine (facing the right shrine).
* '''{{ill|Futodama|Q11059539|qid=Q11059539|lt=Tentadama no Mikoto}}''' (Amenofutodama no Mikoto) - Right shrine (facing left shrine). {{ill|Inbe clan|Q8189229|qid=Q8189229}}Ancestor God.

The two deities enshrined are the gods of Mito (the gods of the port). As far back as the {{ill|Enkyō (Edo period)|Q1183728|qid=Q1183728}} 3rd year ({{ill|1746|Q7589|qid=Q7589}}), in the "Nanki Shrine Record", it appears that the two deities, Hayaakitsuhiko and Hayaakitsuhime, are enshrined {{Sfn|Naru Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=370}}. However, the earlier "Nanki Meishoshi" states that it is unknown, and it is thought that the enshrined deity was unknown in the early {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}{{Sfn|Narujinja (Heibonsha)|1983|p=370}}.Later, in ``{{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|Q11604964|qid=Q11604964}},'' he questioned the theory that two gods were enshrined, Hayaakitsuhiko and Hayaakitsuhime, since there was only one deity enshrined at Narukin Shrine in the ``Engishiki,'' and advocated the theory that Tentadama-no-Mikoto was the enshrined deity.{{Sfn|Narujinsha (Heibonsha)|1983|p=370}}. This speculation is based on the theory that the area around this area is compared to the area of ``Ibe-go'' that appears in ``{{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|Q2702542|qid=Q2702542}}'', and in the same text, it is said that a person lived in this area. {jalink|Ibe clan|Q8189229}} (Kiibe clan) is said to have enshrined its ancestral deity, Tenta Tama no Mikoto {{Sfn|Naru Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=370}}. In addition, the same article states that when Naru Shrine, which had been in ruins, was rebuilt in 4 ({{ill|1719|Q6902|qid=Q6902}}), two deities were considered: Hayaakitsuhiko and Hayaakitsuhime. However, Kii-Ibe is not a family of Inebekushi whose ancestor is Tenta Tama-no-Mikoto, but a family of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kikokuzō}}, and {{ill|Hikosachi no Mikoto|Q135327097|qid=Q135327097}} is its ancestor deity, according to ``{{ill|Kogo Shūi|Q531555|qid=Q531555}}.'' Also, the fourth book of ``Mochizuki'' and ``Sho Keiki,'' which is another name for the founder of Kikuni-zukuri, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takuma Tama no Mikoto}}. </ref>'s father is said to be a Narukami ({{ill|Raijin|Q12808082|qid=Q12808082}}) called {{ill|Raijin|Q12808082|qid=Q12808082}}, and in the Otomo clan genealogy in "Furuya family family history" and "Kamibetsu genealogy," Tenrai no Mikoto is said to be ``Narukami Shrine (Koreya), Nagusa district, Kii province.''<ref name="keifu2">Keninobu Nakata "Shinbetsu Genealogy", {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|Q653433|qid=Q653433}} Digital Library. </ref>.Based on the Tentaitama no Mikoto theory, in {{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}}8 ({{ill|1996|Q2070|qid=Q2070}}), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tentadama no Mikoto Shrine}} ({{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}{{ill|Kashihara, Nara|Q496319|qid=Q496319}}Ibe Town), the spirit of Tentadama no Mikoto was once again solicited and enshrined in the main shrine.<ref name="historical book"/>.

=== History ===

=== Founding ===
According to the shrine biography cited in "Ki Meisho Zue", around the time of {{ill|Emperor Kōan|Q312821|qid=Q312821}} (sixth generation), the god {{ill|Hayakitsuhiko and Hayakitsuhime|fr|Hayakitsuhiko et Hayakitsuhime|ja|ハヤアキツヒコ・ハヤアキツヒメ|ko|하야아키츠히코・하야아키츠히메|simple|Hayaakitsuhiko and Hayaakitsuhime|zh|速秋津日子神與速秋津比賣神|qid=Q11326733|lt=Hayaakitsuhiko-no-Mikoto}}, and Naru-jinja Shrine was founded as a result of this enshrinement. The company name ``Naru'' is said to be a name related to a river, as it is assumed in ``{{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|Q11604964|qid=Q11604964}}'' that it means water flowing from a valley called ``Narumizu'' or ``Narutaki''. {{Sfn|Naru Shrine (Gods)|1986}}On the other hand, {{ill|Jōhei|Q1324874|qid=Q1324874|lt=Shohei}} ({{ill|931|Q24789|qid=Q24789}}-{{ill|938|Q24794|qid=Q24794}}) link|Japanese Ruijusho|Q2702542}}", you can see the entry "Inbe" as {{ill|go|Q130458414|qid=Q130458414}} of Nagusa District.<ref name="Ibego"/>. This is believed to be near Inbe, Wakayama City, south of Narukin Shrine, and the area is said to have been the {{ill|Korean clans|Q846706|qid=Q846706|lt=honkanchi}} of {{ill|Inbe clan|Q8189229|qid=Q8189229}} (Kii Inbe) in Kii. Nagusa District, Ibe-go section, Kobe-go section. </ref>. Also, in the same book, ``Nabe'' appears next to ``Ibe'', but this is a misprint of ``Kobe'', and is thought to mean ``Ibe Kobe'', that is, the god of Inbe (a private house attached to a shrine).<ref name="Ibe-go"/> Relatedly, in the ``Shinshokakuchofusho'' {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daido}} 1st year ({{ill|806|Q30021|qid=Q30021}}), there are mentions of 10 of the 20 households of Inabe deity in Kobe <ref name="Ibego"/>. It is certain that Kobe was located at Naru-jinja Shrine from the description of ``50 bunches of sake rice, divine tax'' in the Shijiki-sai Ainosai article of the ``Engishiki'', so it is thought that these Inabe-Kobe were attached to Naru-jinja Shrine, and Naru-jinja Shrine was enshrined as the guardian deity of Kii Inabe.<ref name="Ibego"/> It is also assumed that these Kobes were distributed around Narukami, Wakayama City, where Narukami Shrine is located <ref name="Ibego"/>.In addition, in "{{ill|Kogo Shūi|Q531555|qid=Q531555}}", Kiibe is a descendant of {{ill|Hikosachi no Mikoto|Q135327097|qid=Q135327097}}, and is the ruler of Nagusa District. It is written that he lived in Kigo and Arakago (neither of which have "Wamyosho") and was responsible for paying tribute of lumber and building palaces and shrines. </ref>.

=== Outline ===
In national history, {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} In the first year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), there is an article about the promotion of {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} from the 8th grade of Jugoi to the 8th grade of Jushii (Junior 4th rank and lower rank) in the first year ({{Sfn|Narujinsha (Heibonsha)|1983|p=370}}.In "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}, {{ill|Kii Province|Q864053|qid=Q864053}}{{ill|Nagusa district|Q11415547|qid=Q11415547}} has "Narujin Shrine Meishin University It will be listed at {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}} as ``Monthly Ainame Shinnai'' and {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|Q11516161|qid=Q11516161}} and {{ill|Ainame Festival|Q11581944|qid=Q11581944}}・It is written that it was deposited in {{ill|Hanpei|Q11481885|qid=Q11481885}} at {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518}}{{Sfn|Narukinsha (Heibonsha)|1983|p=370}}. There are many famous shrines in Kii Province, but the ones that received dedications at the three festivals are Narukinja Shrine, {{ill|Hinokuma Shrine|Q888184|qid=Q888184|lt=Maejin Shrine}}, {{ja There were only four shrines: link|Mae-mae Jingu/Kokukake Shrine|Q888184|Kunikake Shrine}} and {{ill|Itakiso shrine|Q11379271|qid=Q11379271}}. Regarding these four companies, please refer to "{{ill|Ryōshūge|Q11378321|qid=Q11378321}}" Jingirei<ref group="hara">"Reishūkai" Volume 7 (Jingirei) Nakafuyujo Kamiusaōsai. </ref>Also, there is a description that it was listed at Hoheisha Shrine on the occasion of the Aijo Festival on Kami U no Hi in November as ``Mae, Kokukensu, Itaukeso, Narukami'' {{Sfn|Narujinsha (Heibonsha)|1983|p=370}}.In the storage rice book of {{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}}3 ({{ill|1048|Q19359|qid=Q19359}}), 340 steps of Narukami Shrine rice fields can be seen {{Sfn|Narukin Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=370}}. Also, in ``{{ill|Kii no Kuni Jinmyō-chō|Q17210008|qid=Q17210008}}'', it is written as ``Shoichii Naru-Okami'' {{Sfn|Naru Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=370}}.

{{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} In 13 ({{ill|1585|Q6736|qid=Q6736}}), {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Q187550|qid=Q187550}}'s {{ill|Battle of Kishuu|Q10855721|qid=Q10855721}} {{ill|Ōta Castle|Q10941625|qid=Q10941625|lt=Ota Castle}}It is said that during the water attack, the surrounding area, including Narukin Shrine, was greatly devastated. The shrine building was constructed in {{ill|Kyōhō|de|Kyōhō|es|Kyōhō|fa|کیوهو|fr|Ère Kyōhō|ja|享保|ko|교호|ru|Кёхо|simple|Kyōhō|sr|Кјохо|sv|Kyōhō|tr|Kyōhō|zh|享保|qid=Q1145048}}4 ({{ill|1719|Q6902|qid=Q6902}}), and five Kanda shrines were donated {{Sfn|Narujinja (Heibonsha)|1983|p=370}}.

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it was ranked as {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}} in the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine rank system}}. In the 40th year of the Meiji era ({{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}}), in accordance with the ordinance to enshrine shrines, the nearby Shikinai shrines Kenmaon Shrine and Katsuchi Shrine were enshrined within the shrine grounds.

=== Kenmaon Shrine ===
``Katamaoto Shrine'' (Katamanoto Shrine) is a shrine within the precincts of Narukin Shrine. {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old company rank}} is {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}. Currently, it is enshrined together with Kotsuchi Shrine.

The following deities are enshrined:
* Kamiadaka Ashitsuhime no Mikoto {{Sfn|Katsuchi Shrine/Kanmaon Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1987|p=58-59}}
*: Another name for {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|Q1781862|qid=Q1781862|lt=Konohana Sakuyahime no Mikoto}}.

In national history, {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} In the first year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}, he was conferred {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}}, which is the upper rank of Jugoi, and in the seventh year of Jogan ({{ill|865|Q30350|qid=Q30350}}), it was ranked as a government shrine, and in the 8th year of Jogan ({{ill|866|Q23872|qid=Q23872}}), there is a record that it was conferred the rank of Junior Fourth Rank and Lower.{{Sfn|Kanshin Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=370}}."{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}} is {{ill|Kii Province|Q864053|qid=Q864053}}{{jalink |Nagusa District|Q11415547}} is described as "Kanmaon Shrine" and is listed as {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and in "{{ill|Kii no Kuni Jinmyō-chō|Q17210008|qid=Q17210008}}" it is listed as "Shoichii Shrine". ``Arimaon Okami'' is compared to Kenmaon Shrine {{Sfn|Kanmaon Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=370}}. Relatedly, in "{{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|Q2702542|qid=Q2702542}}", "Arima" is mentioned as {{ill|go|Q130458414|qid=Q130458414}} of Nagusa District, and it is determined that it is near Narukami, Wakayama City. </ref>.

Kenmaon Shrine was originally located approximately 300 meters northeast of Naru Shrine {{Sfn|Kanmaon Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=370}}. At his place of birth, there is a monument erected as ``Katsune Shrine Kyoho Kotatsu'', which appears to be inscribed in the year {{ill|Kyōhō|de|Kyōhō|es|Kyōhō|fa|کیوهو|fr|Ère Kyōhō|ja|享保|ko|교호|ru|Кёхо|simple|Kyōhō|sr|Кјохо|sv|Kyōhō|tr|Kyōhō|zh|享保|qid=Q1145048}}9 ({{ill|1724|Q6926|qid=Q6926}}) {{Sfn|Katsune Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=370}}.{{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} April 7th ({{ill|1874|Q7761|qid=Q7761}}), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Modern company rating system}}, {{Sfn|Katsuchi Shrine/Kanmaon Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1987|p=58-59}} listed as {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}. In 1907 ({{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}}), it was relocated to the precincts of Narukin Shrine in accordance with the ordinance to enshrine shrines. Later, a branch spirit was summoned to the shrine in Wakayama City, and the shrine building was rebuilt (currently Kenma-on Shrine, {{Coord|34|12|50.79|N|135|12|9.45|E|region:JP-30_type:landmark|name=Kanma-on Shrine (descendant shrine)}}).

The shrine is as follows.
* Records of {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} dedication in the history of the Six Kingdoms (all written as "Kanma Ongami")
** {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} May 26th, 1st year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), from upper 6th rank to upper junior fifth rank (``{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}'')
** On May 17, 7th year of Jogan era ({{ill|865|Q30350|qid=Q30350}}), he was listed as a government shrine (``Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'')
** Leap March 13, 8th year of the Jogan era ({{ill|866|Q23872|qid=Q23872}}), from the top of the fifth rank to the bottom of the fourth rank (``Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'')
* After Six Kingdoms History
** Shoichii ("{{ill|Kii no Kuni Jinmyō-chō|Q17210008|qid=Q17210008}}") - Written as "Arimaon Okami".

=== Katsuchi Shrine ===
'''Katsuchi Shrine'' (Katsuchi Shrine) is a shrine within the precincts of Narukinja Shrine. {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old company rank}} is {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}. Currently, it is enshrined together with Kenmaon Shrine.

The following deities are enshrined.
* {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|Q1640658|qid=Q1640658|lt=Encounter with Tsuchi no Mikoto}} (Kagutsuchi no Mikoto) {{Sfn|Katsuchi Shrine/Kanmaon Shrine (Shikiuchi)|1987|p=58-59}}
